Round 2 · Implementation · Hard

Ticket #22 — Shared Document Permissions

Difficulty: Hard

Context

You maintain sharing for documents inside nested folders. A direct grant is on the document; an inherited grant comes from its folder or a parent folder. A viewer may read, an editor may read and edit, and the document owner may also share. Revocation denies a user access at a specified scope.

Practice report

Create folder root, its child child, and document d in child, owned by owner. Grant sam editor access on root and viewer access directly on d. Revoke sam on d, then ask for role("d", "sam") and read access.

Observation Current starter Expected
Resolved role viewer None
Read route status 200 403

The document revocation must hold despite the two existing grant sources.

Acceptance Criteria

  • The immutable document owner always resolves as owner and cannot be revoked. Owner, editor, and viewer capabilities follow the read/edit/share levels above.
  • A document revocation denies direct and inherited grants until an explicit document regrant clears it. Revocation must not change another user's access.
  • Otherwise, a document grant wins over inherited grants. Without a document grant, use the nearest applicable folder grant while walking toward the root.
  • A folder revocation blocks inherited access through that scope. A direct document grant can still provide access; it is distinct from inheritance.
  • Resolve by scope, independently of grant insertion order. Folder traversal must terminate even if the supplied folder graph contains a cycle.
  • Unknown documents and unsupported actions are denied. Invalid grants and attempts to revoke an owner do not change existing permissions.

Out of Scope

Keep the existing grant/revoke APIs, role set, and folder graph. Login, organization-wide policies, new actions such as deletion, and redesigning folder storage are outside this ticket.

Investigation

Reproduce the revocation report and compare direct, nearest-folder, and parent-folder grants. Add tests for document and folder revocation, explicit regrant, owner protection, and unsupported actions. Assert both the resolved role and route result after each permission change.
